checked: src/Scans/ (remaining 33 scan files: comment-headed, not docstring-documented, spot-checked)

findings.title: grade()'s exit-code contract omits the pending_state exit-1 case
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:518: "Exit 1 while `open_ids` is non-empty, 0 when every id is closed."
src/CLI/Passes.jl:680-682: `isempty(open_ids) || (...; return 1)` then separately `isempty(pending_state) || (...; return 1)` then `return 0`
findings.description: The docstring states a binary contract (1 iff open_ids non-empty, else 0), but the code has a third path: when open_ids IS empty yet pending_state is non-empty (ids the blind verifier was never asked about this pass), grade() still returns 1, not 0. A reader would believe 'no open_ids' guarantees exit 0, which is false whenever ids are still pending_state.
findings.resolution_hint: State the contract as three-valued: exit 1 when open_ids is non-empty OR pending_state is non-empty; exit 0 only when both are empty.

findings.title: close()'s "2 on a stamp mismatch" is true for only one of three stamp mismatches
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:867: "Returns 0 when closed, 1 when a condition is unmet, 2 on a stamp mismatch."

src/CLI/Passes.jl:890-894: config_sha and tool_version mismatches are pushed onto `fails` (exit 1 unless regraded); only `tool_tree_sha != rec["tool_tree_sha"]` while the version is unchanged returns 2 directly
findings.description: Of the three stamps close() checks, only a tool_tree_sha mismatch under an unchanged tool_version (the tag moved) triggers the documented exit 2. A config_sha or tool_version mismatch instead joins `fails` and yields exit 1. In a package whose CLAUDE.md states 'Exit codes are the contract', this misstates that contract.
findings.resolution_hint: Narrow the claim to name which stamp mismatch causes 2 (the tag-moved case) versus which merely joins `fails` and causes 1.

findings.title: classify_lane()'s enumerated :dead causes omit the zero-findings/empty-checked[] case
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:326-327: "The status is `:dead` (absent, or — renamed to `<name>.rejected.json` beside itself — unparsable or invalid)"
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:349: `(n == 0 && isempty(get(data, "checked", []))) && return (:dead, data, sha, "zero findings AND empty checked[] — a dead lane, not a clean one")`
findings.description: The docstring lists exactly two ways a lane file becomes :dead — absent, or a rename-and-quarantine on unparsable/invalid content. It omits a third path that is the direct realization of RULE.TEST.MISSING_IS_FAILING central to this package's design: a well-formed lane file with zero findings AND empty checked[] is also :dead, with no rename involved.
findings.resolution_hint: Add the zero-findings/empty-checked[] case to the :dead enumeration, distinguishing it from the quarantine-rename cases.

findings.title: usage() prints a different exit-2 meaning than main()'s own docstring states
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl:108: `println(io, "usage: gbg [--dev] <noun> [<verb>] [options]   (exit 0 clean · 1 finding · 2 a second finding · 3 crash)")`
src/CLI/Main.jl (main's docstring): "returns that function's exit code: 0 clean, 1 substantive finding, 2 cannot evaluate, 3 crash"
findings.description: Every other statement of the exit contract in this codebase reads 2 as "cannot evaluate". The literal text usage() prints to users instead reads "2 a second finding", contradicting main()'s own docstring for the function that prints it.
findings.resolution_hint: Fix the usage() string to read "2 cannot evaluate".

findings.title: cmd_install()'s "Returns 0 when both files are written" is false for the default invocation
locations: src/CLI/Install.jl:38: "Returns 0 when both files are written, 2 when the Julia in use is below the floor..."
src/CLI/Install.jl:53-65: the `~/.gbg/dev` pointer is written only `if haskey(o.values, "dev-checkout")`; without that flag only the shim is written, yet the function still returns 0
findings.description: `gbg install` run without `--dev-checkout` (the common case) writes only the shim file, never the dev-checkout pointer, and still returns 0. The docstring's stated success condition — "both files are written" — is not the actual condition for exit 0.
findings.resolution_hint: Reword to "Returns 0 when the shim (and, with --dev-checkout, the pointer) is written".

findings.title: bank()'s "Any DEAD lane ⇒ exit 2" undercounts what actually blocks banking
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:428: "Any DEAD lane ⇒ exit 2 and nothing frozen (`lane_shas` stays). Returns the exit code."
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:445-450: `dead = [k for (k, s) in statuses if s in (:dead, :rejected)]` then `if !isempty(dead) ... return 2`
findings.description: The same docstring distinguishes DEAD from REJECTED as two of four statuses, then its closing sentence says only 'Any DEAD lane ⇒ exit 2', reading as excluding REJECTED. In the code, a REJECTED lane blocks banking exactly like a DEAD one.
findings.resolution_hint: Say "Any DEAD or REJECTED lane ⇒ exit 2" to match the code and the rest of the same docstring.

findings.title: release()'s closure criterion understates what cites_round() actually accepts
locations: src/CLI/Release.jl:44: "the `/check-docs` round opened at the latest `<ver>-rc.<n>` tag is closed by honored or adjudicated ids"
src/CLI/Release.jl:25: `get(e, "closed_by", nothing) in ("honored", "adjudicated", "rescan", "seeded") || String(id) in carried`
findings.description: release()'s docstring lists only two of the four closure dispositions cites_round() actually accepts (honored, adjudicated) — it omits rescan and seeded, and that an id in the round's own `carried` list also counts as satisfied.
findings.resolution_hint: Either list all four channels plus carried, or cross-reference cites_round()'s own (accurate) docstring instead of restating a narrower list.

findings.title: init()'s unconditional refusal of an existing config.toml does not hold under --dry-run
locations: src/CLI/Init.jl (init's docstring): "It refuses an existing `.gbg/config.toml` (exit 2). Returns the exit code."
src/CLI/Init.jl:242: `isfile(cfgpath) && !dry_run && (println(io, "init: $cfgpath exists; ..."); return 2)`
findings.description: The refusal is explicitly gated on `!dry_run`. With `--dry-run` and an existing config.toml, init() does NOT refuse — it proceeds to preview, contradicting the docstring's unqualified refusal claim.
findings.resolution_hint: Add the dry-run exception explicitly: "refuses an existing config.toml, except under --dry-run, which previews regardless".

findings.title: prepare()'s docstring documents seeding for check-consistency but is silent on the identical behaviour for check-docs
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:134-136: check-consistency paragraph names seeding explicitly; check-docs paragraph does not
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:195: `haskey(rec, "seed_salt") && (seed_docs_corpus!(cfg, round, dir, rec; io) == 0 || return 2)`
findings.description: prepare()'s check-docs paragraph never mentions seeding, even though a seeded check-docs round also has prepare() copy the lane surfaces into a disposable corpus and plant seeds there — a real side effect that can itself fail and return exit 2. The check-consistency paragraph documents the analogous behaviour; the check-docs one does not.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a clause to the check-docs paragraph noting the seeded-round corpus copy, mirroring the check-consistency paragraph.

findings.title: page_bindings()'s docstring omits the id-attribute fallback the code actually uses
locations: src/Scans/html_docstring_once.jl:7: "the binding anchor's target (its `href` without the `#`)"
src/Scans/html_docstring_once.jl:22: `id = lstrip(HtmlWalker.attr(n, "href", HtmlWalker.attr(n, "id")), '#')`
findings.description: The docstring says the id comes from the anchor's href. The code actually falls back to the anchor's id attribute when href is absent — a fallback never mentioned, and one an adjacent code comment ('not in an id attribute') sits oddly beside.
findings.resolution_hint: Either document the fallback, or drop the dead code if href is genuinely always present.
